# KPro v0.2.0 candidate

This is a release preparation draft. The version is not published by adding
this file. Complete the release checklist before tagging.

KPro remains a pre-1.0 Go multi-transport application framework. This minor
release includes source-incompatible changes from v0.1.0.

## Changes

- Security dependency updates: Go 1.26.9, x/net v0.60.0, x/text v0.42.0,
  and gRPC v1.83.2. Transitive dependencies are updated to the versions
  required by this dependency graph.

- Dependency-neutral server assembly through explicit transport construction
  and `Mount`, `MountNative`, `MountNativeChecked`, or `MountRunner`.
- Optional message write receipts, outbound drain, aggregate outbound
  snapshots, and a shared live transport conformance suite.
- Contract-first service scaffolding, gRPC addition to an existing service,
  typed OpenAPI clients, contract catalogs, and local declarative templates.
- TCP fault-injection coverage and opt-in stress and soak workflows.
- TCP queue drains respect `MaxWriteBatchFrames` under backlog. Applications
  that relied on the previous implicit doubling should review batch sizing.

## Upgrade from v0.1.0

Upgrade to Go 1.26.9 or newer before building. Go 1.25 is no longer supported
in this minor release because the updated security dependencies require Go
1.26. The CLI, scaffolding templates, and CI baseline use the patched toolchain.

Construct each transport in its own package and replace removed
protocol-specific `server.Server` convenience calls with explicit mounting.
Follow [the golden path](https://github.com/saramand9/kpro/blob/v0.2.0/docs/golden-path.md) and
[quick start](https://github.com/saramand9/kpro/blob/v0.2.0/docs/quickstart.md) at the same revision as the module.
Regenerate starter projects only after reviewing generated-file ownership;
do not overwrite an existing application with a new scaffold.

Use the CLI, framework module, and documentation from the same version.
Source-mode scaffolds use a local module replacement; remove it and pin the
published version before distributing an application.

## Adoption boundaries

Pin a reviewed version. Validate capacity, slow consumers, failure recovery,
shutdown, and downstream dependencies against the target workload. Write
receipts report transport writes, not peer processing or durable business
delivery. Authentication and authorization belong to the application or gateway.
Production-v1 acceptance remains incomplete; see the
[roadmap](https://github.com/saramand9/kpro/blob/v0.2.0/docs/production-v1-roadmap.md) and
[release preparation checklist](https://github.com/saramand9/kpro/blob/v0.2.0/docs/open-source-release.md).
